Is it appropriate to bring an iced coffee to a job interview? That’s the debate that’s been making the rounds on the internet after a recruiter criticized Gen Z candidates for arriving to interviews with one in hand, prompting a wider argument about whether the drinks look unprofessional. In a recent piece for Forbes, senior contributor Benjamin Laker, who serves as professor of leadership at Henley Business School, University of Reading, in the U.K., breaks down why the debate is about more than just coffee. According to Laker, the discussion “shows how quickly an interviewer’s preferences about dress, greetings and body language can harden into standards candidates were never told about.” While job interview etiquette can vary depending on industry and setting—a remote interview may not be as formal as an in-person panel interview—Laker acknowledges that coming to an interview prepared, on time, and with honest answers are the standard rules to follow. But he admits that in recent years, rules around appearance and manners have become a little less clear-cut, leading to blurred lines between what interviewees think is appropriate and what interviewers actually expect.  “Remote interviews and less formal offices have made some old cues harder to interpret,” Laker writes. “Employers should be able to explain which expectations relate to the work. Candidates should notice when the answer is simply, ‘That’s how we do things here.’” Below are a few of Laker’s tips on how to decide which job interview rules you should follow depending on the format, industry and location of your interview. Deciding What To Wear: Laker advises candidates to use the role they are interviewing for as a reference point. “Clean, understated sneakers may fit a casual technology or creative workplace; polished shoes may be safer in a conservative or client-facing setting,” he writes. “If you’re unsure, ask the recruiter what candidates typically wear. Choose something appropriate that lets you concentrate on the conversation.” Deciding To Bring Coffee Or Water: “Water offered by the host is easy to accept or decline,” writes Laker. “If you bring coffee, finish it before entering if practical. If not, ask whether it’s all right to carry it in. The aim is to keep the drink from interrupting the exchange.” Deciding To Communicate More Formally Or Casually: Laker advises job

79998.subject: StonkFun September Spike
79998.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

StonkFun is a Solana launchpad that lets anyone price a new token in almost any asset, from tokenized stocks and project tokens to SOL, stablecoins or its own STONK token. Launches run on Raydium's LaunchLab bonding curve and graduate into Raydium pools. 

When StonkFun moved its launches onto Raydium's LaunchLab on Sep 5, revenue went from $38K a day to $1.40M a day in the following week and peaked at $2.48M on Sep 11. As the chart below shows, it took ~32% of revenue across the 13 launchpads tracked from Sep 6 to 28, second only to Pump's ~42%, and even briefly out-earned Pump on Sep 11.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5c257950-1fd5-4746-be3f-2d3870bde421/image.png?t=1790768464)
Caption: 

The initial differentiator was the quote asset. On Pump almost everything was priced in SOL. On StonkFun, 39% of last week's launches were priced in tokenized stocks, ETFs or pre-IPO names. Pump added a similar feature within a week, adding Custom Pairs on Sep 9, yet it has taken only 21% of stock-paired launchpad trading on Solana since. 

The other draw was the reward drop. Most StonkFun launches carry a 1% or 3% transfer tax that is paid out to holders in the quote asset several times a day, so holding a meme paired with NVDAx drips tokenized Nvidia into your wallet. Around $80M has been paid out through Sep 28. However, Pump's Holder Rewards, live Sep 12, now does the same from trading fees.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b986e560-dc16-409d-995b-9b16313bee28/image.png?t=1790768464)
Caption: 

Revenue has been fading much like Pons's did. The chart below indexes each launchpad's daily revenue to its own peak day (Pons Sep 5, StonkFun Sep 11) and the curves sit almost on top of each other: 17 days out StonkFun was at 22% of peak, Pons was at 20% at the same point and is 11% today. 

That highlights how cyclical launchpad revenue is, especially when competing with an established player like Pump. Notably, 68% of StonkFun's revenue comes from tokens under a day old, and the last three days averaged $537K.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5d345664-9db6-46e2-8eac-867a1357b9c1/image.png?t=1790768464)
Caption: 

However, valuation still prices STONK as a short-term fade. To build confidence in the token, about 60% of revenue buys and burns STONK, with nearly 19% of the supply already gone and the current pace annualizing to almost 100% of market cap.

As the final chart shows, STONK trades at ~0.6x trailing 30-day sales at ~$200M marke

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin is clinging to its best September on record even as Treasury yields hit multi-decade highs. Meanwhile, Wall Street keeps building on-chain rails while US regulators run on a skeleton crew. 📈 Bitcoin Eyes Best September on Record as Bond Yields Bite Bitcoin is up about 7.3% in September, fractionally ahead of 2024's 7.29% and on course for its best September since 2013, provided it closes the month above roughly $83,600. The push comes despite a bond-market selloff that drove the US 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since 2007, while spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their inflow streak to nine straight sessions. Read full story 🛡️ Bitget Restores USDT Withdrawals After $387M Hack Bitget has reopened BTC, ETH and USDT withdrawals following its $387.5 million breach, with fiat, P2P and remaining tokens scheduled to return Friday. Its first post-hack proof-of-reserves snapshot shows all 19 covered assets above 100%, and CEO Gracy Chen says the User Protection Fund is back above $300 million. More details ⚖️ SEC and CFTC Shrink to Three Commissioners as Peirce Exits Hester Peirce, the SEC's "Crypto Mom," leaves the agency on Friday, leaving Chair Paul Atkins and Mark Uyeda as its only commissioners. With Michael Selig running the CFTC alone, just three officials will steer US crypto oversight across both regulators, as the White House says nominations are coming soon. Read more 🏛️ Cboe and S&P Dow Jones Eye Tokenized S&P 500 Options Cboe Global Markets and S&P Dow Jones Indices renewed their exclusive S&P 500 options licence for another 25 years, through 2051, and flagged possible collaboration on tokenized options contracts. The idea is still exploratory, but it links a franchise that traded a record 970.6 million contracts in 2025 to blockchain infrastructure. See details 🏦 Morgan Stanley Opens Digital Asset Lab for Stablecoins and DeFi Morgan Stanley has set up a Digital Asset Lab within its innovation-lab network to test stablecoins, tokenized deposits, CBDCs, tokenized money-market funds and DeFi vaults, isolated from its core banking systems. The effort, led by Megan Brewer, does not yet give clients access to any of these products.
